domain_restrictions: a and b are integers with 0 <= a <= b.
r and j are nonnegative integers.
I is finite because it consists of the integers from a+1 through b.
Every i in the product lies in I, hence i is a positive integer since a >= 0.
S must be a subset of I.
lambda must be a finite multiset whose elements all lie in I.
The symbol |lambda| means the sum of the multiset elements, not the number of elements.
The constraint for membership in X_j is |lambda| plus the sum over s in S of r+s equals j.
The coefficient extraction [q^j] is understood in the formal power series sense.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integers a, b, r, j with 0 <= a <= b and r, j nonnegative, let I be the set of integers from a+1 through b and let F be the finite product over i in I of (1 minus q to the power r+i) times the geometric series in q to the power i. Then the coefficient of q to the j in F equals the sum over all pairs (S, lambda) where S is a subset of I and lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I whose element-sum plus the sum of r+s over s in S is j, with each pair weighted by minus one to the power of the size of S.
quantifier_order: For all integers a, b, r, j satisfying 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0 and j >= 0.
Define I as the integers from a+1 through b.
Define F as the finite product over i in I of (1 minus q to the power r+i) times the geometric series sum over m >= 0 of q to the power m i.
Define X_j as the set of pairs (S, lambda) with S a subset of I and lambda a finite multiset of elements of I such that the total sum of lambda plus the sum of r+s over s in S equals j.
Then the coefficient of q to the j in F equals the signed sum over X_j of minus one to the power of the size of S.

witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses outside the indexed pairs in X_j; the statement is an equality of two expressions for each fixed a, b, r, j.
Membership in X_j depends jointly on S and lambda through the same total weight j.
The summand depends only on S through its cardinality, but the indexing set also counts all admissible lambda with the required total sum.

statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and j >= 0. Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. Define the formal power series F_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i in I} ((1 - q^(r+i)) * sum_{m>=0} q^(m i)). Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then [q^j] F_{a,b,r}(q) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^(|S|).
